clues: This town lies in the south of Spain, just west of Málaga. It sits on the west shore of a bay, with a hill range right behind it.
Summers here are long and dry, while winters stay mild but can bring short bursts of heavy rain. Sea winds from Africa also blow in fine dust from the Sahara.
Long a poor fishing village, this place changed in the late 1950s. Tourism began then, and it became the first beach resort on its sunny coast.
In 2017, this town shared a huge world Pride fest with Madrid. Its own Pride each June is now the third biggest in all of Spain.
Its beach runs for close to five miles along the sea. A bright, lit path runs beside it, lined with small beach bars that serve food and drinks.
